neighbours.label: ' the' (or the first letter) right before the proper name of a river, spring or landmark in historical / topographic description ('the bed of the Tiber', 'from the Gihon spring'); the - pole fires on prehistoric stone monuments and earthworks
fire: The ruined priory stands on the south bank of the Severn, a mile below the weir.
The basilica rises in a stately way from the bed of the Tiber, close to the island.
For centuries the lower pool was fed by water from the Siloam channel.
The legion crossed the plain and pitched its camp on the bank of the Rhine, near the ford.
The eastern wall of the fortress drops straight into the bed of the Tagus, below the old bridge.
The monastery was founded on the north bank of the Tweed, near the border.
The lower town grew up along the bank of the Thames, beside the Roman wall.
The old mill stood for centuries in the bed of the Avon, just above the abbey.
quiet: The ruined priory stands on a low hill, a mile from the nearest farm.
The basilica rises in a stately way from a paved square, close to the market.
For centuries the lower pool was fed by rainwater from the roof gutters.
The legion crossed the plain and pitched its camp at the edge of the woods, near a well.
The eastern wall of the fortress drops straight into a dry ditch, below the old gatehouse.
The monastery was founded on the edge of the moor, far from any road.
The lower town grew up around the cattle market, beside the old wall.
The old mill stood for centuries at the end of the lane, just above the orchard.

notes: Card: ' the' x13 before Tiber, Vltava, Tabernacle, Sopwell, Gihon. Probes: bank of the Thames 0.42, bed of the Arno 0.31, Gihon 0.27, Jordan 0.16, Danube 0.13, Loire 0.06; everyday 'the' 0.03-0.06. Median may fall just under 0.20.
